why: Defending an attacked work and repeatedly repairing the same work are hard to separate when the same pixels are vandalized and restored.

why.T3-068: The concepts propose altering an existing Canadian or Chilean flag into Peru's own flag, which is converting a neighbour's art rather than destroying it or adopting it unchanged.

why.T3-002: The item is dominated by calls for hands, joining, and asking people to help with the Autobot/Decepticon symbols; other themes present are named under also_present.

why.T3-164: The concepts frame the flag as giving identity and visibility and leading someone to discover the sub, matching feeling supported or visible through the canvas rather than national pride or recruitment.

why.T3-005: The concepts contain alarms and calls to defend the flag and heart under attack or vandalism, so defending the work against attackers leads.
why.T3-021: Other concepts treat the heart and flag as something to repeatedly restore and reinforce after vandalism, which is watching and repairing distinct from a fight call.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-005 alone would not carry the repeated repair and restoration of the heart and flag after vandalism when no distinct fight is being called.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0133326 and C0821152 show repeated restoring and reinforcing of the heart and flag, satisfying T3-021's watch-and-repair gate with its own repair concepts.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-021 if forced; the loss would be the ongoing repair and keep-it-intact aspect.

why.T3-073: The concepts look back on the finished flag by recounting the ordeal, pacts, waiting, and a missed chance to help, which is reporting what happened to the work rather than celebrating or announcing it.

why.T3-023: The concepts center on the Transformers Discord's moderators changing the server to a Gobots Discord for April Fools, with members reacting inside that changed venue, which is an April Fools takeover rather than testing an outside claim.

why.T3-074: The concepts show builders compensating for too few hands with VPN magic, joining, repair calls, and backing each other, which is working around the few-hands problem while building.
why.T3-136: The concepts also explicitly doubt the room's capacity, saying only about five people are doing the flag and a bigger design is hard with so few.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-074 alone would not carry the explicit doubt and estimates that the room is too few for the work.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0989992 and C0167400 state the small number of builders and comparison to other small groups, satisfying T3-136's doubt-of-strength gate.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-136 if forced; the loss would be the explicit capacity doubt.

why.T3-029: The concepts mourn the Peruvian Pikachu after takeover or erasure, including RIP and a joking minute of silence, so mourning the lost work is the leading act.

why.T3-020: Many concepts choose starting points, corners, and bases for the flag on the canvas, which is choosing a spot.
why.T3-004: Other concepts settle the flag's look and scale: making it smaller, plain red-white-red, writing Peru first, and adjusting text and border.
why.T3-070: The remaining concepts give coordinates, plans for the emblem, border improvements, and expansion directions for placers to follow.
